title: The RSI(2) dip rule on SPY since 2001 won 71% of its trades and still finished $17k behind buy and hold
author: person-person12
selftext:
RSI(2) is the Larry Connors rule that half of trading YouTube still teaches for SPY. You buy when the 2 day RSI drops under 10 and sell when price closes back above the 5 day average.

I ran the plain version in [Agenticks](https://www.agenticks.ca/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=post&utm_campaign=autopilot&utm_content=ai_trading) on SPY daily candles from January 2001 to March 2026, starting with $10k. It buys the next open after the signal and sells the next open after the exit close. Commission and slippage are charged on every trade, and dividends are left out.

**$10k finished at $32,324.** That came from 301 trades with 71.4% winners, a profit factor of 1.67 and a worst drop of 31.2%.

Holding SPY over the same window finished at about $49,200 and sat through a 56.5% drop. So the rule gave up roughly **$17k of ending balance** to take about 25 points off the worst drawdown.

The costs are the part people skip when they quote this one. Across the 301 round trips they came to **$2,283, a bit over 9% of what it made** before costs. Thats at 3 cents a share of slippage and 50 cents commission a side, so a sloppier fill eats more of it.

The very first trade shows why people like it, bought Jan 3 2001 and sold the next day for +$506. The losers look like March 2001, when it bought a dip that kept dipping for two weeks and gave back $322. There is no stop in the rules, so nothing cuts a trade like that short if the dip turns into a real crash.
